pultec-low-boost-c19-floated.vrt / .dump
========================================

A low-boost board carrying ONE part that is off the board: C19, which was at
hole 3,13 and is FLOATING. Nothing else differs from the committed layout.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS COMMITTED RATHER THAN REGENERATED
---------------------------------------------------------------------
It is the negative fixture for the H3 / H8 gates of
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-stripboard-pipeline-design.md - a board that
every term of the pipeline's cost objective reports as healthy while one of its
parts is in mid-air. Its CUT count is 5, its NODE count is 9 and its GRID is
14 32, exactly as on the committed layout; the only two dump signals that differ
are the PART line's placement field and the absence of C19's two PIN lines, and
both derive from Component::GetIsPlaced(), so they are one signal reported twice
rather than two witnesses.

It is committed, and cannot be regenerated, because the only thing that ever
produced such a board was a shipped verb exiting 0 while floating a part - which
is the defect M1.2 removes. Spec section 4 names this sequencing trap: capture
the fixture from the pre-M1.2 binary first, because afterwards no shipped verb
will make one. This capture is that one.

HOW IT WAS MADE - the exact commands, on a scratch copy, never on a board under
boards/
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  cp boards/pultec-low-boost/pultec-low-boost.perfboard.vrt $SCRATCH/low.vrt
  veroroute --stretch $SCRATCH/low.vrt --ref C19 --direction grow -o $SCRATCH/s1.vrt
  cp $SCRATCH/s1.vrt tests/fixtures/pultec-low-boost-c19-floated.vrt
  veroroute --dump-board tests/fixtures/pultec-low-boost-c19-floated.vrt \
      > tests/fixtures/pultec-low-boost-c19-floated.dump

The stretch exited 0, printed nothing on stdout and nothing on stderr, and wrote
the board. That is the whole of the defect.

PROVENANCE OF THE INPUT, AND THE BINARY THAT WROTE THE OUTPUT
-------------------------------------------------------------
  input board      boards/pultec-low-boost/pultec-low-boost.perfboard.vrt
                   at commit 2f62ee1d643e15e73bd220c10215957ab4c460a9
                   sha256 411412bdf087c5aeea15195ae6ffc2bd1e453c3ca81fcdcf64307effd21b43ae
  this fixture     sha256 89049aaec626d7864e702701bff36d52cf8df1791aa7a0011c4da66ec6978b13
  binary           .tools/veroroute-perfboard at commit
                   2cfaad8171cd9a2be881117d19f4d748e8e1a4a0, which is what
                   veroroute.pin pins, built from that commit
                   (.tools/veroroute-perfboard/.built-commit agrees)

The .dump beside it is this binary's --dump-board output on this file, committed
for the same reason tests/fixtures/pt2399-core-board.dump is: it is the readable
form of the board, and a test can assert over it without spawning the binary.

WHAT MAY NOT BE CONCLUDED FROM IT
---------------------------------
It is not evidence about any other board, and it is not a layout. C19's grow was
refused by Board::CanPutDown because the wider footprint collided with occupied
holes; the part being off the board is that refusal's symptom, not a placement
anybody chose.
